title: Who will bring the light of peace?
takeaway: When darkness spreads, someone has to go and find the light.
scene: This ghazal is printed in two columns, and each row is one couplet. It mixes heartbreak with worry about a country sliding into darkness and cruelty.

original: اوہدے نے ہاسے یار تڑفا رہے نیں
میریاں سدھراں نوں جو موتی لا رہے نیں
transliteration: Ohde ne haase yaar tarfa rahe nain
Meriyaan sadhraan nu jo moti la rahe nain
translation: Friends, it's the beloved's laughter that's tormenting me,
the laughter that strings pearls onto my longings.
couplets.story: The Beloved's laughter hurts him. Each laugh feels like a pearl added to his string of wishes: beautiful, but it makes him want them even more.

original: امن دی روشنی کدھروں لے کے آؤ
ہور ظلم دے ہنیرے ودھدے جا رہے نیں
transliteration: Aman di roshni kidhron lai ke aao
Hor zulm de hanere vadhde ja rahe nain
translation: Bring the light of peace from somewhere,
because the darkness of cruelty keeps growing.
couplets.story: He pleads: someone, please find the light of peace and bring it here. The darkness of cruelty keeps spreading.

original: تاہنگ جنہاں دی اکھیاں عمر وہائی اے
اوہو ہتھیں اج مینوں دفنا رہے نیں
transliteration: Taangh jinhaan di akhiyaan umar vahaai ae
Oho hatthin ajj mainu dafna rahe nain
translation: The ones my eyes spent a lifetime longing for
are the very hands burying me today.
couplets.story: He spent his whole life longing to see certain people. Now they've finally come, but only to bury him.

original: شمع دی لاٹ دا کھلیکھا او دیکھو
اوہدے مکھ دے ول پتنگے جا رہے نیں
transliteration: Shamaa di laat da bhulekha o dekho
Ohde mukh de val patange ja rahe nain
translation: Look at that: mistaking it for a candle flame,
the moths are flying toward the beloved's face.
couplets.story: The Beloved's face glows so brightly that moths fly toward it, thinking it's a candle.

original: اوہنوں روکو حشر نہ برپا ہو جاوے
گھنڈ مکھڑے توں اپنا کیوں سرکا رہے نیں
transliteration: Ohnu roko hashr na barpa ho jaave
Ghund mukhre ton apna kyon sarka rahe nain
translation: Stop them, or Judgment Day might break out!
Why are they slipping the veil off their face?
couplets.story: He jokes: stop the Beloved from lifting the veil. If people see that face, it might cause the end of the world.

original: ظلمت دا اے زور ڈاہڈا دھرتی تے
زروالے تے چن تے کوٹھے پا رہے نیں
transliteration: Zulmat da ae zor daadha dharti te
Zar-vaale te chann te kothe pa rahe nain
translation: Darkness has a terrible grip on the earth,
while the rich are building houses on the moon.
couplets.story: Darkness and injustice have a strong grip on the world. Meanwhile the rich are so busy with their own ambitions it's as if they're building houses on the moon.

original: میرے کہن تے کوئی تے مالی نوں پچھے
باگ دے پھل تے کلیاں کیوں کملا رہے نیں
transliteration: Mere kehan te koi te maali nu puchhe
Baagh de phull te kaliyaan kyon kumla rahe nain
translation: At my request, will someone please ask the gardener
why the garden's flowers and buds are wilting?
couplets.story: He asks someone to go and question the gardener, the people in charge. Why are the flowers and young buds of the garden, the people and the young, wilting?

original: بحر ہجر وچ ڈبدا کیہڑا بچ دا اے
لہراں وچہ سفینے ڈولے کھا رہے نیں
transliteration: Behr-e-hijr vich dubda kehra bachda ae
Lehraan vich safeene dole kha rahe nain
translation: Who drowning in the ocean of separation ever survives?
Ships are rocking in the waves.
couplets.story: Nobody who sinks into an ocean of missing someone ever makes it out. Even big ships are tossing in those waves.

original: کیہڑا وید طبیب ایہہ سانوں دسے گا
دلاں دے درد چھنے دودھ دے جا رہے نیں
transliteration: Kehra vaid tabeeb eh saanu dasse ga
Dilaan de dard chhinne duddh de ja rahe nain
translation: Which doctor or healer will explain this to me:
the pains of the heart keep spreading, like milk curdling?
couplets.story: As a doctor himself, he asks which healer can explain it. Heart pain spreads through people the way milk curdles.

original: نویں چولے چیرے کئیاں بدلے نیں
نویں رنگ وچ ویکھو لٹن آ رہے نیں
transliteration: Naveen chole cheere kaiyaan badle nain
Naveen rang vich vekho luttan aa rahe nain
translation: Many have changed into new robes and turbans;
look, they're coming to rob us in new colours.
couplets.story: Many people have put on new clothes and new turbans, new looks and new slogans. Don't be fooled. They're the same thieves, coming to rob people in a new disguise.

original: کویں لنگھی رات ہجر دی اے احمدؔ
تیرے ہنجو تے جگراتے چغلی کھا رہے نیں
transliteration: Kiven langhi raat hijr di ae Ahmad
Tere hanjhu te jagraate chughli kha rahe nain
translation: Ahmad, how did the night of separation go?
Your tears and your sleepless eyes are telling on you.
couplets.story: He asks himself: how did that lonely night go, Ahmad? He doesn't need to answer. His tears and tired eyes give it away.

deeper: The moths flying to the Beloved's face, mistaking it for a candle, is the classic Sufi image of the soul drawn to God's light. Most of this poem, though, is social conscience: leaders in 'new robes' who keep robbing the people, and a garden wilting under careless gardeners. Asking for 'the light of peace' in a darkening land is a prayer as much as a protest.
why: The line about thieves in new clothes, the same people with new slogans, is just as true today.
prompt: How can you tell when someone is just wearing 'new robes' rather than actually changing?
notes: Printed in two columns; each row is read as one couplet.
Couplet 9, line 2: 'chhinne duddh de' is read as curdling milk, a loose reading that needs checking.
